html:
The American zone was the part of defeated Germany that the United States occupied from 1945 to 1949: Bavaria, Hesse, the north of Württemberg and Baden, and the port of Bremen as a supply base.

The Americans ran the occupation from Frankfurt and pushed denazification hard, with millions of questionnaires and tribunals. The main war crimes trial of Nazi leaders was held at Nuremberg, in the zone, in 1945 and 1946. They also set up new German state governments early and held local elections from 1946.

By 1947 Washington had decided that a working German economy was needed to rebuild Europe and hold back Soviet power. The zone merged economically with the British one, the Marshall Plan brought aid, and the currency reform of June 1948 put goods back in the shops. When the Soviets answered with the Berlin Blockade, American planes kept West Berlin supplied for almost a year. In 1949 the zone became part of West Germany, within Allied-occupied Germany as a whole.
sum: The American zone was the part of defeated Germany that the United States occupied from 1945 to 1949: Bavaria, Hesse, the north of Württemberg and Baden, and the port of Bremen as a supply base.
